dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: North Steps and Canal Walk have four library windows to share. This route machine runs a small practice schedule with the rule and request counts you give it. A draft claims the desk heard every request. Walk beyond the desk and bring both slips back.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The desk sheet recorded twelve and five. The walking round brings three and eleven more after repeated request numbers are set aside. Keep one rule in the machine while you swap the input. At the weir, you held one setting steady to see what the repair changed.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: You held the rule steady. It ran with seventeen requests from the desk and thirty-one when the walking slips joined it. Both numbers belong to the way they were collected. Now hold the joined tally steady and change the rule to see who gets the windows.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The same joined tally can give different windows to the two districts. The machine follows the rule you give it. Take your two results to Lin so the public notice carries the rule as well as the numbers.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The desk opens during the workday. The walking crew speaks to people as it goes. Bring both collection slips to Ade. Try one rule first on the desk record and then on the joined record. Next, try a second rule on the joined record.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The joined tally reads fifteen for North Steps and sixteen for Canal Walk. A starting window at each keeps both places on the first schedule. A queue rule follows the larger count. An equal split gives both the same number. Put a rule you tested on the public notice.

options.text: Send all four windows to the larger recorded queue.
Leave one starting window in each district, then give the larger count the other two.
Give each district two windows.
Leave the route open for now.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The printed rule and count are beside the desk. A reader left a reply on the Canal Walk rail. They needed something the count could not show.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: One request number tells us a request was made. The reader at Canal Walk has to find a stop at a time they can reach. The window counts leave that question open. Keep the first rule in view and give the next request round a place and a time to check.

options.text: Leave an evening request stop with a time-and-place line.
Give the walking crew a place-and-time line for its next round.
Leave the notice ready.
I kept a separate waiting tally at the Nexus bench.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: At the Nexus, the tray recorded a loan move. Your waiting tally kept a different count. Here the route ledger records requests. A person waiting for an evening window still needs a way to leave that detail. Keep both kinds of record where readers can check them.

options.text: Leave an evening request stop with a time-and-place line.
Give the walking crew a place-and-time line for its next round.
Leave the notice ready.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: Lin sends a place-and-time card to Canal Walk for an evening round. The first four window counts stay on their own dated line by the public desk. A reader finishing work later can tell the crew where and when to meet before the next schedule is drawn.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The walking crew carries a second sheet past the canal stairs. People can give a reachable place and time during the next round. The four window counts remain on the wall while the crew gathers the new details.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: A reader at the low bench can find both district names. The rule, counts and open schedule details run together on the small card. Shall we leave them their own lines?

options.text: Leave a wider route notice at the low bench.
Keep the notice where it is.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The wider sheet gives the trial rule, each district’s count and the next place-and-time check their own lines. A reader can go back to the line they need.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The wider sheet leaves room for the next evening or walking record. Someone at the bench can follow how the first four windows were shared and where to leave a reply.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: The plan sends all four windows to Canal Walk, which has sixteen recorded requests. North Steps has fifteen and gets zero in this trial. Lin leaves that count and the zero together on the door. A reader has room to add a question below.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: One window goes to North Steps, three to Canal Walk. The first window lets each district begin on the plan. The extra two follow the larger recorded count. Lin leaves room for a question about when they will happen.

dialogue.speaker: civic-clerk
dialogue.text: Both districts get two. The notice puts the equal split alongside the two different counts so a reader can see the rule did the sharing. Lin leaves a clip under the notice for the next reader.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: Three sealed load slips are clipped to the red tray. Each slip gives one courier’s practice arrival. This desk can take one load at each numbered mark.

options.text: Unclip the three slips and place their loads.
Leave the clips in place.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: Three sealed load slips are clipped to the blue tray. Each slip gives one courier’s practice arrival. This desk can take one load at each numbered mark.

options.text: Unclip the three slips and place their loads.
Leave the clips in place.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: Two loads land on the first mark. Leave one beside the desk to wait. The fourth mark takes the last load. Two marks remain empty. The cart has three loads and four places in the shift, but one place is needed twice.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The first, second and fourth marks each take one load. The third stays empty. All three couriers clear the desk as they arrive.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The two trays show different outcomes. This rack holds every ordered arrival for three named couriers. Each courier gets the same four slips to draw from, and you put the slip back before the next draw.

options.text: Start filling the rack with rows that keep all three loads apart.
Leave the rack empty.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The first courier gets four choices. Slide their used mark out of the row. Three choices remain for the second courier and two for the third. With the marks all back in play, each of the three can choose any of the four.

options.text: Group the remaining rows where two or more loads share a mark.
Leave the rows ready.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The shared-mark rows fill more than half the rack. If every ordered row has the same chance, exactly five out of eight have a match. This counts matching arrivals in the model. The crew’s bell slip can tell us whether their shifts let the arrivals spread evenly.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The two trays tested what this desk does to known arrivals. The rack counts matches when the marks are equally likely and each draw is independent. The bell slip ties real couriers to the same release. Try a receiving arrangement for one practice shift.

options.text: Ask a helper to take a second load beside the busy mark.
Give the three couriers separate marks and keep one spare.
Leave the arrangement open for now.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: A helper takes a spare crate bracket to Canal Walk. If three loads reach that mark together, someone still has to wait. The first practice tray stays in the hall to compare.

dialogue.speaker: civic-operator
dialogue.text: The North Steps clerk pins three separate marks to the practice stand. The counts guarantee room if the assigned marks hold. A spare mark gives someone with a changed shift a place to try.

missions.knowledgeQuestion: How do the people we count and the rules we use shape the service others can reach?

missions.title: A Notice Within Reach
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How does a notice help someone find the line they actually need?

objectives.title: Give the rule, counts and next check more room on the notice.

missions.title: Three Loads, Four Marks
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When can a chance model guide a receiving plan, and where do arrivals need to be observed?

objectives.title: Load both sealed practice trays at dispatch.
Group the possible arrivals and check the crew’s release time.
Try a receiving arrangement and visit the installed practice setup.

journal.text: Changing the recorded requests changed the route under the same rule. We kept the first window counts beside the rule and asked where and when readers can reach the stops.

In the equal, independent draw model, 40 of 64 ordered arrivals shared a mark. The fixed trays showed whether three known loads fit. The crew’s shared release time changed what it was reasonable to assume about actual arrival times.

chronicle.title: Four windows on a notice
chronicle.text: The public board gives both district counts and the rule that shared the four library windows.

chronicle.title: Places and times still open
chronicle.text: A reader asked which window they could reach. The next request round will leave room for a time and a place.

Visit Route Clerk Lin at the North Steps desk.

Put the four windows on the notice and read the public result by the desk.

Two sealed trays wait at Library Dispatch.
One tray is near the west passage. The other is near the cart beside the east passage.
Unclip the slips and place the three loads on each tray.
Use the red tray, then the blue tray. Compare loads waiting with empty marks.
Check the counting rack and find out when the couriers can leave work.
The four-mark rack is in Dispatch. The crew’s slip is at the Canal Walk bench.
Make the separate rows in the rack, then group the rows that share an arrival mark.
Fill both sets of rows at the rack. Read the end-of-shift slip at Canal Walk.
The practice dispatch board has room for one receiving arrangement.
Use the board near the east side of Library Dispatch.
A helper can take a second load at one mark. Separate reservations need times people can actually use.
